standard_prerequisites.name: Having enough points for a site
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Sites, the notion of a site with enough points, i.e. of a conservative family of fibre functors given by morphisms from the point
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the property asserted for the fourteen sites listed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Comparison of the topologies and geometric points of a scheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the description of points of the etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies by geometric points of the scheme, and the standard facts that the affine versions and the big versions have the same points
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the argument that the listed sites have the same conservative families of points.

core_obligations: Reduce to the small etale site (proof lines 3821-3832): the author observes that the sites in the list are related by the comparison of topologies, so that a conservative family of points for one of them provides one for the others.

Identify the points (proof lines 3832-3840): geometric points of S give points of all the listed sites, and the resulting family is conservative because a map of sheaves is an isomorphism if and only if it is so on all geometric points, which is the exactness theorem for stalks.
proof_roadmap: Use the comparison of topologies to pass between the listed sites.
Take the family of points given by the geometric points of S.
Use the stalk exactness theorem to see that this family is conservative.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that fourteen sites attached to a scheme, the small and big Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf sites together with their affine versions, each have enough points (statement lines 3810-3819). The proof uses the comparison of the topologies to reduce the assertion to one of the sites (proof lines 3821-3832) and then observes that the geometric points of S supply a conservative family of points for all of them, because a map of sheaves is an isomorphism exactly when it is so on all stalks at geometric points (proof lines 3832-3840). The non-formal content is the reduction through the comparisons of topologies. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one identification of points.
